actions.label: Manage food disbursement through FWB staff and FWB-selected local assistants
Hand over distribution to existing guard and militia structures
Supply ongoing food aid deliveries to the camp's refugees
Lobby the SML and Ministry of Defense for funds for guard salaries and generator costs
Provide food rations to guards and their families as compensation
Require distribution documentation forms for donor accountability
Permit and provide security for FWB's independent nutritional assessment
Accept coordinated, escorted presence in the camp with no free movement
Allow FWB staff or FWB-selected local assistants to manage the food distribution
Run the food distribution through guard and militia structures
Refrain from skimming or confiscating FWB food for guards
Grant FWB staff coordinated, escorted access to the camp to deliver and monitor food

goals.label: An independent nutritional assessment and related procedures are carried out in the camp
Food aid is used as currency, payment or traded and resold
Food aid reaches intended refugees without diversion, skimming or confiscation
Guards and their families are fed and compensated, keeping them loyal and disciplined
Aid is documented and accountable as donors require
Camp authorities and militia control food distribution
Commander's authority and appearance of strength
FWB controls food distribution through its own staff or selected local assistants
FWB neutrality is preserved and aid is not used as payment or leverage for armed actors
FWB staff access the camp and move freely to deliver and monitor aid
FWB staff and assistants are safe from threats and violence
Food is distributed impartially and equally without excluding any group
Funds from the SML and Ministry of Defense arrive for camp operations and debts
Generators keep running with fuel and parts
Refugees stay contained in the camp and do not reach the capital
Refugees suffer abuse, violence or collective punishment
The camp receives an ongoing supply of food aid
Control over the narrative and information about the camp
Suspected terrorists in the camp are excluded from food and kept under control

redLines.label: Prioritize hiring local host-community actors for distribution activities
redLines.quote: If FWB hires local independent laborers for the food distribution, you cannot trust those people not to stir unrest and even potentially support hidden terrorists by sharing items or information.

redLines.label: Hire local host-community workers or partners such as MASHA

assumptions: Commitments are binding and additive.
Goals and goal-action links were each extracted 3 times by a model; only those found in a majority of runs are kept.
Actions are chosen to bring about as much goal value as possible, within the solver's size limit.
Our values are the median of stances elicited from our role card.
The opponent column is the expected value of an elicited stance distribution (shared documents only); each opponent reading is one draw from it, independently per goal.
Stance labels map to numbers by a fixed scale (game.stance_values), not a measured utility.

Red lines and must-haves come from our role card, each with a verbatim quote. No plan may include a red-line action, leave out a must-have, or pass through a state worth less to us than our BATNA (the bottom line).
